text: Chapter 20 recommends immutability as the strategy that makes most of this difficulty disappear. Which difficulties, specifically?
choices: Unintended aliasing, defensive copying, mutable map keys, and thread safety — all of them presuppose that something can change.
The equals/hashCode contract, since immutable objects need neither method.
Only the map key problem, since immutability fixes hashing but not aliasing.
Debugging difficulty, since immutable objects can be printed at any time safely.
explanation: Each of the four is a question of the form *could this have changed since I last looked?*, and immutability answers it in advance. Chapter 31 promotes the argument from clarity to correctness: a program with no shared mutable state cannot have a race, and that property is established by reading rather than by testing.
